segments.voice: Yesterday, reading the Gita's first chapter: kuladharmah sanatanah, a family's long-standing ways, and a long word split at its seam. Now the chapter reaches its last verse.

Anyone who has ended up on a bedroom floor beside something unfinished, phone face down, already knows how chapter one of the Gita ends. No battle. A man sits down. Arjuna lowers himself onto the floor of his chariot and lets his bow go. That much is plain. The puzzle comes one line later, in the label the chapter wears at its end. It calls all of this a yoga. The yoga of Arjuna's despair. Why would anyone name a collapse that way?
screen: `THE BEDROOM FLOOR.` → `NO BATTLE. A MAN SITS DOWN.` → `WHY CALL DESPAIR A YOGA?`

segments.voice: First the verse: evam uktvarjunah sankhye rathopastha upavishat, visrijya sasharam chapam shokasamvignamanasah. Uktva: having spoken, the -tva ending that says one thing happened before the next. Visrijya: having let go, the -ya ending doing the same job. Upavishat: he sat down. Having spoken, having let go of his bow with its arrows, he sat down. That's the same staircase of grammar Duryodhana used near the start, when he walked up to his teacher and spoke. Duryodhana's staircase climbs to a speech. Arjuna's goes down to the floor. Then one long compound. Split it: shoka, grief; samvigna, shaken; manasah, the mind. His mind shaken by grief. Now the puzzle. After the verse comes a closing line that isn't part of the dialogue, the chapter's colophon, its label. It ends: arjunavishadayogo nama prathamo 'dhyayah. The yoga of Arjuna's despair, by name, the first chapter. Vishada is despair, and the chapter is named for it. Here's the solution as far as the text goes: the label names the chapter and says nothing more. Some readers hear in the word yoga a hint that despair can be the start of a path. Others hear it simply as the heading each chapter wears. Either way, the despair is chapter one, not the last chapter.
screen: `UKTVA, VISRIJYA: HAVING SPOKEN, LET GO.` · `UPAVISHAT: HE SAT DOWN.` · `SHOKA: A MIND SHAKEN BY GRIEF.` · `VISHADA: THE CHAPTER'S NAME.`

segments.voice: Sit down fully, the way Arjuna does, and let your hands rest open on your knees, as if something heavy has just been set down. Let the shoulders drop on each out-breath. Nothing to carry for now.
Reading the Gita's first chapter, to its last line: uktva, having spoken, upavishat, he sat down, and vishada, despair, the name the chapter carries.
